paragraphs.title: The Heading and the Cry to God

easy.explanation: He says, “I cried unto God with my voice.”
easy.q: To whom does the psalmist cry?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “he gave ear unto me.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask God to do?

easy.explanation: The repetition emphasizes the psalmist’s direct and personal appeal to God.
easy.q: What is emphasized by repeating “with my voice”?

answers: The cry is answered by God’s attention
medium.explanation: The psalmist cries to God, and God gives ear to him.
medium.q: What is the relationship between crying and God giving ear?

medium.explanation: The thought is repeated twice in verse 1.
medium.q: How many times does the psalmist say “I cried unto God”?

answers: He is speaking to the people
medium.explanation: The repetition shows earnest and urgent prayer.
medium.q: What does the repeated wording suggest about the psalmist?

answers: A cry, repetition, and a request for God’s attention
A storm, a battle, and a victory
A song, a journey, and a sacrifice
challenge.explanation: The opening moves from crying to God to asking Him to hear.
challenge.q: Which sequence best describes the opening verses?

answers: They relate to speaking and hearing
challenge.explanation: The psalmist speaks, and God listens.
challenge.q: What do “voice” and “gave ear” have in common?

challenge.explanation: The psalmist immediately brings his trouble directly before God.
challenge.q: What does the direct address to God reveal?

paragraphs.title: Nighttime Distress and Lack of Comfort

answers: In the day of his trouble
easy.explanation: He says, “In the day of my trouble I sought the Lord.”
easy.q: When did the psalmist seek the Lord?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “my soul refused to be comforted.”
He says, “Thou holdest mine eyes waking.”
easy.q: What happened to the psalmist’s eyes?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes trouble that continued through the night.
medium.q: What does “my sore ran in the night, and ceased not” communicate?

answers: Trouble, lack of comfort, sleeplessness, and silence
medium.explanation: The verses portray emotional distress, wakefulness, and inability to speak.
medium.q: Which sequence best describes the psalmist’s condition?

medium.explanation: He says, “I am so troubled that I cannot speak.”
medium.q: Why could the psalmist not speak?

answers: Emotional pain affecting comfort, sleep, and speech
challenge.explanation: The distress reaches his soul, eyes, and ability to speak.
challenge.q: What accumulates in the description of distress?

challenge.explanation: His soul refuses comfort, and his trouble does not cease.
challenge.q: Which condition remains unresolved during the night?

answers: Distress affects both his body and expression
challenge.explanation: His sleeplessness and inability to speak both show the depth of his trouble.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the connection between waking eyes and silence?

paragraphs.title: Reflection on the Past and Questions About God’s Kindness

easy.explanation: He says, “I have considered the days of old.”
easy.q: What past period does the psalmist consider?

easy.explanation: He says, “I call to remembrance my song in the night.”
easy.q: What does he remember at night?

answers: Whether He will cast off for ever
easy.explanation: He asks, “Will the Lord cast off for ever?”
easy.q: What does he ask about the Lord?

medium.explanation: The question concerns whether God’s mercy has permanently ended.
medium.q: What does “his mercy” refer to in this passage?

answers: Whether God has rejected, ceased showing favor, or forgotten mercy
Whether the clouds will pour rain
Whether Moses will lead the people
medium.explanation: The psalmist asks several painful questions about God’s continued favor.
medium.q: Which group of questions appears in these verses?

medium.explanation: His distress causes him to reflect and question God’s apparent absence.
medium.q: What leads the psalmist to ask these difficult questions?

answers: Remembering the past while feeling rejected in the present
Watching the sea and the clouds
challenge.explanation: The psalmist remembers earlier times while wondering whether God has cast him off.
challenge.q: What is the central tension in these verses?

answers: Hath he in anger shut up his tender mercies?
Will the Lord cast off for ever?
Doth his promise fail for evermore?
challenge.explanation: “Tender mercies” directly refers to God’s compassion.
challenge.q: Which question most directly concerns compassion?

answers: From memory to questions about rejection, mercy, and compassion
challenge.explanation: The psalmist begins with remembrance and moves into painful questions about God’s kindness.

paragraphs.title: Choosing to Remember God’s Deeds and Wonders

easy.explanation: He says, “I will remember the works of the LORD.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist decide to remember?
What does he remember from ancient times?

answers: His people, the sons of Jacob and Joseph
easy.explanation: The verse names the sons of Jacob and Joseph as God’s redeemed people.
easy.q: Whom did God redeem with His arm?

answers: The years of the psalmist’s life
medium.explanation: The psalmist meditates on and speaks about God’s deeds.
medium.q: What does “thy doings” mean in context?

answers: He turns his attention toward God’s works
medium.explanation: He deliberately focuses on God’s wonders and actions.
medium.q: What change occurs when the psalmist says, “I will remember”?

answers: Wonders, works, deeds, strength, and redemption
medium.explanation: The psalmist recalls God’s wonders, works, strength, and redemption.
medium.q: Which sequence best summarizes the passage?

answers: It turns his thoughts from doubt toward God’s power and redemption
It keeps him focused only on the night
challenge.explanation: Remembering past wonders gives him a foundation for hope.
challenge.q: How might remembering God’s works help the psalmist?

answers: The psalmist moves from uncertainty to recognition of God’s power
He moves from the sea to the desert
He changes from prayer to war
challenge.explanation: He answers his troubled thoughts by recalling God’s mighty deeds.
challenge.q: What change occurs between questioning God’s mercy and declaring His wonders?

answers: His revealed strength is shown in saving His people
They both refer to musical instruments
challenge.explanation: God’s strength is demonstrated through the redemption of His people.
challenge.q: How are God’s strength and redemption connected?

paragraphs.title: A Powerful Revelation in Water and Storm

easy.explanation: The verse says, “The waters saw thee, O God.”
The depths were troubled by God’s presence.
The verse says, “The clouds poured out water.”
easy.q: What did the clouds pour out?

medium.explanation: The depths are the deep parts of the waters.

answers: The waters’ fearful response and the storm
The leadership of Moses and Aaron
medium.explanation: The passage begins with waters, depths, clouds, thunder, and lightning.
medium.q: What is described first in these verses?

answers: The skies’ sound and the voice of thunder
medium.explanation: The skies send out a sound, and thunder has a voice.
medium.q: What sounds are mentioned in the storm?

challenge.explanation: The trembling earth and storm display divine power.
challenge.q: What does the storm reveal about God?

answers: As responding with fear and disturbance
challenge.explanation: The waters are afraid and the depths are troubled.
challenge.q: How are the waters and depths portrayed?

answers: They make God’s powerful presence visible and audible
challenge.explanation: The storm gives dramatic expression to God’s revelation.
challenge.q: Why are thunder and lightning important in the passage?

paragraphs.title: God’s Way Through the Sea and His Guidance of the People

easy.explanation: The verse says, “Thy way is in the sea.”
The verse says, “thy footsteps are not known.”

easy.q: How did God lead His people?

answers: God can make a way through overwhelming places
God was defeated by the waters
medium.explanation: The image presents God as sovereign over the great waters.
medium.q: What does “thy path in the great waters” suggest?

answers: His leading of the people by Moses and Aaron
medium.explanation: The final verse describes God guiding His people through their leaders.
medium.q: What is described after God’s way in the sea?

answers: God’s care and guidance of His people
medium.explanation: A flock depends on its shepherd for direction and care.
medium.q: What does the flock image emphasize?

answers: It is real, yet His footsteps leave no visible trace
It is made by Moses alone
challenge.explanation: The verse says God’s footsteps are not known.
challenge.q: What is unusual about God’s path through the sea?

answers: God displays power in creation and care in guiding His people
Both images describe the psalmist’s sleeplessness
challenge.explanation: The passage joins God’s cosmic power with His personal leadership.
challenge.q: What connection exists between the sea and the flock?

answers: From the hidden path in the sea to the ordered guidance of the people
From silence to a musical heading
challenge.explanation: The ending moves from mysterious divine power to shepherd-like leadership.
challenge.q: What is the major movement at the end of the psalm?
